A_target.statement:
Let $A_1, A_2, \ldots$ be [[Definition:Event|events]] with $\displaystyle \sum_n \map \Pr {A_n} < \infty$.
Then:
:$\displaystyle \map \Pr {\limsup_{n \mathop \to \infty} A_n} = 0$
that is, [[Definition:Almost Surely|almost surely]] only finitely many $A_n$ occur.

B_source.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a [[Definition:Measure (Measure Theory)|measure]] and $E_1, E_2, \ldots$ measurable.
Then:
:$\displaystyle \map \mu {\bigcup_i E_i} \le \sum_i \map \mu {E_i}$

substitutions.the sets E_i: the tail events A_n for n >= N

object_map.reformulation: Bound the limsup event by each tail union, and the tail union by the tail of a convergent series.

validity_conditions: Convergence of the series is what makes the tail sums tend to 0.
proof_plan: $\displaystyle \limsup_n A_n = \bigcap_N \bigcup_{n \mathop \ge N} A_n \subseteq \bigcup_{n \mathop \ge N} A_n$ for each $N$.

By monotonicity and the source result:
:$\displaystyle \map \Pr {\limsup_n A_n} \le \sum_{n \mathop \ge N} \map \Pr {A_n}$
As the series converges, its tails tend to $0$ as $N \to \infty$.

Hence $\map \Pr {\limsup_n A_n} = 0$, which is the first [[Borel-Cantelli Lemma]].
{{qed}}
